origin.description: Create an ordered series of observations, including an irregular time series.
origin.usage: zoo(x = NULL, order.by = index(x), frequency = NULL, calendar = getOption("zoo.calendar", TRUE))

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A numeric vector, matrix, or factor. A shorter or longer vector is recycled to the length of the index.

arguments.name: order.by
arguments.text: Index vector by which the observations are ordered. Duplicate entries are kept, with a warning.

arguments.name: frequency
arguments.text: Numeric frequency of the index. When it matches the index spacing, the result is a regular series of class zooreg.

arguments.name: calendar
arguments.text: When frequency is 4 or 12, store a numeric index as yearqtr or yearmon.

origin.details: Observations are stored with an index attribute and sorted by order.by. A zero-length numeric series may keep an index of any length. A frequency that does not lie on the index grid is ignored. A vector prints horizontally and a matrix prints vertically.
origin.value: A vector or matrix ordered by an index of the same length as the number of rows.

translation.description: Create an ordered series of observations, including an irregular time series.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A numeric vector or matrix. NumPy holds the values, and a matrix is stored in Fortran order. A shorter or longer vector is recycled to the length of the index.

arguments.name: order_by
arguments.text: Index vector by which the observations are ordered. Duplicate entries are kept, with a warning.

arguments.name: frequency
arguments.text: Numeric frequency of the index. When it matches the index spacing, the series is marked regular.

arguments.name: calendar
arguments.text: When frequency is 4 or 12, snap a numeric index the way yearqtr or yearmon does.

translation.details: Observations are stored with an index and sorted by order_by. A zero-length numeric series may keep an index of any length. A frequency that does not lie on the index grid is ignored. A vector prints horizontally and a matrix prints vertically.
translation.value: A Zoo series ordered by an index of the same length as the number of rows.
translation.example:
import math
import sys

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, "/home/ahmed/killr_projects/killr/packages/zoo")
from zoo.zoo_class import aggregate_zoo, ifelse_zoo, is_zoo, median_zoo, quantile_zoo, rev_zoo, xtfrm_zoo, zoo


def show(value):
    if isinstance(value, (bool, np.bool_)):
        print("TRUE" if value else "FALSE")
        return
    if is_zoo(value):
        show(value.data)
        show(value.index)
        return
    array = np.asarray(value, dtype=float).ravel(order="F")
    print(" ".join("NA" if math.isnan(float(item)) else format(float(item), ".16g") for item in array))

show(zoo([1, float('nan'), 3], [1, 2, 3]))
